summary: SciMac is a third-generation, women-owned manufacturer founded in 1956 that machines PTFE labware and cuts precision threads in glass, quartz and ceramic from a 10,500 sq ft plant in Middlesex, NJ. It sells a catalog of PTFE stirrer bearings, stoppers, stopcocks and valves through a WooCommerce store to lab, medical, pharma, semiconductor and food customers, while custom and prototype work is quoted manually by phone, email or web form. Customer service is staffed only 8:30-5:30 EST weekdays, with no chat, booking or quoting automation visible on the site.

facts.fact: Founded in 1956 by Edwin Phillips; described as a third-generation family business and currently a women-owned PTFE manufacturer.
Operates a 10,500 square foot production facility at 700 Cedar Avenue, Middlesex, NJ 08846.
Core services are precision PTFE machining/fabrication plus custom diamond-wheel threading of borosilicate glass, quartz and ceramic, from roughly 4-6mm capillary up to 150mm tooled glass flanges.

PTFE parts were made exclusively for the scientific glassware industry from 1956 to 1995; today products also serve medical, pharmaceutical, oil & gas, electronic, perfume, food and semiconductor markets.
Customer service hours are Monday-Friday 8:30AM-5:30PM EST, with main phone 732-356-1553, toll-free 800-641-7940 and fax 732-356-2569.
Quote requests are taken by web form, phone or email, and the fax line is described as available 24 hours.
The site runs a full e-commerce catalog with cart, checkout, customer accounts, saved product lists, wishlist and a downloadable customer credit application (net-terms/wholesale flow).
Separate application pages exist for becoming a distributor and for educator discounts.
Equipment listed includes CNC machines, vertical milling machines, lathes, hydraulic presses, Royal Master and Glebar centerless grinders and welding machines.
Stated capability limits include ultra-thin walls to .001 inch, taper held under .0001 inch end to end, and parts as small as .010 inch OD.
There is no careers page: https://scimac.com/careers/ returns HTTP 404 and the site's page sitemap lists no employment/careers URL.
The RSS feed contains no posts, indicating the site publishes no blog or news content.

Page source shows WordPress with WooCommerce 11.2.2, Gravity Forms 2.9.27 (with a zero-spam add-on), Yoast SEO Premium 28.7, Advanced Woo Search Pro, YITH wishlist, Woo Discount Rules Pro and an Authorize.Net CIM payment gateway extension.

operations_signals: Order intake is split between self-serve e-commerce checkout for catalog items and manual quote handling for custom work, with no online quoting or configurator tool observed (https://scimac.com/request-quote/).

Custom work is explicitly human-routed: customers are told to call or email so a customer service associate can guide selection or assess whether custom fabrication is possible (https://scimac.com/request-quote/).
Customer service is staffed 8:30AM-5:30PM EST Monday-Friday only; the only stated after-hours channel is a 24-hour fax line (https://scimac.com/contact-us/).

The FAQ page is dominated by sizing and part-identification questions and repeatedly routes users to 'email or call customer service', including for cross-referencing another manufacturer's part number (https://scimac.com/faqs/).
Physical footprint is a single 10,500 sq ft plant in Middlesex, NJ, positioned by the company as central to its markets for fast delivery (https://scimac.com/company/).

Wholesale and institutional buying is supported by a downloadable credit application, distributor application and educator discount application rather than automated account provisioning (https://scimac.com/apply-for-credit/).

Catalog pages are variable-product SKU tables (joint size, color, length, price) with no per-product customization fields, so engineered-to-order requests leave the site (https://scimac.com/products/adapters/inlet/key-head-stopper-standard-taper-full-length-ptfe/).
hiring_signals: No hiring page exists on the company site; /careers/ returns a 404 and no employment page appears in the page sitemap (https://scimac.com/careers/).

No company-specific job postings surfaced when searching regional job aggregators for the business name; results were unrelated employers in the Middlesex area (https://www.talent.com/jobs?k=scientific+machine+supply&l=Middlesex%2C+NJ).
The business appears to recruit without a public careers funnel, so likely roles (CNC machinist, glass threader, customer service/quoting) are not externally visible (https://scimac.com/company/).
review_themes: No customer reviews are displayed on the product pages reviewed, so no product-quality or service themes could be collected (https://scimac.com/products/adapters/inlet/key-head-stopper-standard-taper-full-length-ptfe/).
The site's review sitemap contains no review URLs, consistent with an unused on-site review feature (https://scimac.com/reviews-sitemap.xml).
The business links to Facebook only via a generic Facebook search URL in its page metadata rather than a managed profile, so no social review content is reachable from the site (https://scimac.com/).
tech_footprint: WordPress + WooCommerce 11.2.2 storefront with custom 'starterpistol' theme, variable products and quantity controls (https://scimac.com/).
Advanced Woo Search Pro installed for catalog search, suggesting a large SKU set that needs search assistance (https://scimac.com/).
Gravity Forms 2.9.27 with a zero-spam add-on powers quote, credit, distributor and educator-discount forms; no CRM integration is visible in page source (https://scimac.com/).
Authorize.Net CIM payment gateway extension handles card payments, implying conventional B2B card purchasing rather than punchout/EDI (https://scimac.com/).
No analytics tag, live chat, chatbot or scheduling widget appears in the page source of the home page (https://scimac.com/).
Yoast SEO Premium 28.7 structures metadata and schema; product and page sitemaps are maintained, with product sitemap last modified in October 2026 (https://scimac.com/product-sitemap.xml).
Contact data is exposed as plain phone, fax and info@ email with a single contact form; no customer portal beyond My Account order history (https://scimac.com/contact-us/).
growth_signals: Deliberate diversification since 1995 from scientific glassware only into medical, pharmaceutical, oil & gas, electronics, perfume, food and semiconductor end markets (https://scimac.com/company/).
Catalog is actively maintained: the product sitemap shows items last modified through 2025 and 2026, including newer PTFE stirrer shaft/agitator SKUs (https://scimac.com/product-sitemap.xml).

Two channel-building programs are published - distributor applications and educator discounts - pointing to expansion through resellers and academic accounts (https://scimac.com/apply-to-become-a-distributor/).

Positioning has shifted toward higher-spec industries, with claims of Fortune 500 customers and ultra-thin-wall/tight-tolerance work that suit semiconductor and pharma buyers (https://scimac.com/company/).
The site is now branded around 'SciMac' with a 2026 logo asset refresh, while core content pages still carry 2024 modification dates (https://scimac.com/).
decision_maker: Unknown - no current owner, president or GM is named on scimac.com. The company page names only founder Edwin Phillips (1956), which is historical rather than current leadership.

inferences.inference: Quote intake and part-selection support are handled manually by a small customer-service team, making response speed a likely bottleneck.
inferences.reasoning: There is no configurator, chat or online quote engine; the request-quote page directs users to call/email for guidance, the FAQ repeatedly routes sizing and cross-reference questions to customer service, and service hours are limited to weekday business hours at one 10,500 sq ft plant.

inferences.inference: A large share of inbound inquiries are repetitive product-identification questions that an AI assistant grounded in the catalog and FAQ could deflect.
inferences.reasoning: The FAQ is almost entirely 'how do I measure X', 'what size stopper fits my flask', and 'can you cross-reference another maker's part number', and the answer given for each is to contact customer service.

inferences.inference: The business likely has a few dozen employees rather than hundreds, with machining roles filled through informal channels.
inferences.reasoning: Single 10,500 sq ft facility, no careers page or public postings, and a single info@ inbox with one customer-service phone line; headcount is not published, so this is an estimate, not a sourced figure.

inferences.inference: Catalog data quality and enrichment is a live operational task, not a one-time project.
inferences.reasoning: The WooCommerce product sitemap lists a large number of product URLs with staggered last-modified dates into 2026, and the site runs Advanced Woo Search Pro plus discount-rule and wishlist plugins that depend on consistent product metadata.

inferences.inference: After-hours demand is probably leaking because inquiries can only land in email or fax outside 8:30-5:30 EST.
inferences.reasoning: No chat, no scheduling tool, and the only 24-hour channel advertised is a fax line, while the site sells to national/global industrial and lab buyers across time zones.

data_gaps: Employee headcount and revenue are not published; no company size figure could be sourced.
No current owner/GM/president name is published on the company website, so the decision-maker is unknown.
Job postings could not be verified: Indeed, LinkedIn and ZipRecruiter returned HTTP 403 to automated access, and no company careers page exists.
Public review content could not be retrieved: Yelp, BBB, YellowPages and ZipRecruiter blocked automated access (HTTP 403), and no on-site reviews are displayed.
Web search providers were unavailable during this run (rate limits/errors), so news coverage, awards, expansions and press mentions could not be searched.
No ERP, accounting, shipping or inventory system is visible from the public site; only the web stack could be observed.
Customer concentration and contract/manufacturing volume split (stock catalog vs custom) are not disclosed.
